# Eclipse Launcher Beta 4 — cosmetics hotfix

This update fixes a Minecraft startup crash in the cosmetics bridge and allows cosmetics agents to update independently of the launcher.

## Fixed

- Fixed the Identifier factory lookup that crashed Fabric 1.21.11 while Minecraft loaded internal cosmetic resources. The fix is included in the Java 8, 17, 21 and 25 agents.
- Unsupported identifier APIs leave Minecraft's original resource list intact instead of attaching an unusable provider.
- Fixed the installer's whole-number size metadata and added a real packaged-install smoke check to release builds.

## Cosmetics updates from the CDN

- Each online Minecraft launch checks the CDN content revision. A newer agent is downloaded, checked against its SHA-256 and size, and used for that launch.
- Unchanged agents are reused. A stale manifest cannot downgrade a newer verified cached agent.
- Agent JARs use separate versioned filenames so an update does not replace a file another Minecraft process has open.
- If the CDN is unavailable or a download fails validation, Minecraft uses the last verified agent. Offline launches use the cache, with the fixed bundled agent available for recovery.
- Online skin, badge and cape selections still come from the skin server; the local agent is the renderer, not the authority for account selections.

## Before testing

Install this launcher update before testing the cosmetics fix. Beta 3 restores its embedded cosmetics agent; deleting skinlib alone does not replace that agent. After updating, close and relaunch Minecraft to load the new renderer.

The fixed agents passed 60 Java unit tests, all four supported Java runtime fixtures, and real Minecraft resource-manager checks including Fabric 1.21.11. These checks do not replace testing the beta testers' full modpacks and gameplay.
